name: Interarch Building Solutions Ltd
title: Interarch Building Solutions Ltd - 544232 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Interarch FY26 revenue rose 31% to Rs 1,898 crore; FY27 guided to Rs 2,150-2,200 crore, with order book at Rs 1,700 crore.
summary.overview: FY26 revenue reached Rs 1,898 crore (up about 31% YoY) and EBITDA Rs 176 crore (margin 9.3%), with PAT of Rs 135 crore. Q4 revenue was about Rs 500 crore (up 8.7% QoQ), with volumes near 41,000 tons and EBITDA of Rs 53 crore at a 10.5% margin, which management said was held down by about Rs 5-5.5 crore of one-offs (labour code provision, export certifications, outsourced high-rise engineering, bid costs). Capacity is fully utilised, so growth depends on new plants: the Gujarat PEB plant (fifth integrated plant) targets July 2026 commercial production, and the Andhra heavy structure plant starts in July-August. Management said Q4 was lower than the expected seasonal step-up because Q3 had already run at full capacity; cash flow from operations turned negative in FY26 due to milestone-based receivables and inventory build-up.

financial_highlights.change: +25% YoY vs Rs 108 crore; tax rate about 27% in FY26 vs 24% prior year

financial_highlights.value: Over Rs 1,700 crore, to execute in about 9 months
financial_highlights.change: About 3.2% YoY per analyst; Rs 1,650 crore QoQ per management

segments.name: Pre-engineered buildings (PEB)
segments.commentary: Order book of Rs 1,700 crore is almost entirely PEB; realisation about Rs 120 per kg. Realisation was higher in Q4 and may fall Rs 4-5 per kg as steel prices soften.

segments.name: Heavy structures (HSS)
segments.commentary: Not yet in revenue. First heavy structure order (Rs 102 crore, Delhi Rajpath government building) announced, with supply from September 2026. Realisation about Rs 95-100 per kg, as only structure is supplied without secondaries or cladding.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export revenue about 3-3.5% of total, with Rs 30-35 crore of export orders in hand for FY27 execution. Management targets Rs 100 crore of export orders, and says North America margins are higher.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guided to Rs 2,150-2,200 crore (about 13-16% growth), with no heavy structure revenue assumed in the initial figure.
FY28 revenue target of Rs 2,500 crore; management said it may include heavy structures and will revisit guidance after Q2 or by end of the year.
Net PAT margin guided at 7-7.5% for FY27; EBITDA margin expected around 9.3-9.5% on an annual basis.
Heavy structure plant (Andhra) expected to sell 10,000-12,000 tons in FY27 (Rs 120-130 crore), with full capacity of 18,000-20,000 tons (Rs 200-210 crore a year).
Capacity to reach about 60,000 tons by Nov-Dec 2026 after Gujarat and Andhra phases; capacity of about 180,000 tons a year cited.
Plans to raise funds via QIP within two to three months, mainly for heavy structures.
capex_capacity: Gujarat PEB plant (fifth integrated plant, about Rs 2,500 crore capacity): building complete, machinery installation from first half June, trial production June, commercial production July 2026; Phase 2 machinery by end-2026. Delay of about 1-1.5 months was due to high water table requiring foundation redesign.
Andhra Pradesh heavy structure plant: Phase 1 in July-August 2026; Phases 2 and 3 planned to be accelerated, targeting completion around end of next year. Machinery imported from Germany and Italy.
Current capacity about 160,000 tons (four plants) plus outsourcing, quoted at about 180,000 tons a year; running at about 40,000 tons a quarter.
Additional land bought in Gujarat for a second PEB or heavy structure plant; combined planned capacity of Rs 3,000 crore PEB and Rs 500 crore heavy structures.
Canadian partner JV for 100% export unit (open web joist) under MoU signed 20 May 2026; plant expected in about a year (around August-September 2027).
demand_pricing: Pipeline 1 (orders expected within 60 days) about Rs 800-900 crore; Pipeline 2 (bid, decision in 2-7 months) about Rs 3,500 crore, mainly PEB.
Order intake limited by delivery capacity; management said it would not take orders it cannot deliver and sees no demand slowdown.

Steel supply: no disruption to projects per management; relationships with SAIL, JSW and AMNS cited. Labour shortage in March (LPG crisis, elections) cost about Rs 20-25 crore of revenue, now back to normal.

Cash flow from operations turned negative in FY26 due to larger milestone-based orders (Rs 100 crore plus) and steel inventory built ahead of price rises; management expects it to turn positive quickly.
Margins: management targets 9.5-10% EBITDA over time and cites hidden costs of new businesses; said North America exports offer better margins.

qa_highlights.question: Steel supplier concentration and whether disruptions hit Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there were no project disruptions; steel suppliers were stable through long relationships. The Q4 shortfall was driven by labour shortages in March, not steel supply.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue impact from site clearance delays in the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the impact was about Rs 20-25 crore, with the quarter only held back to avoid spoiling material.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the order book not growing and how does the pipeline look?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said orders are capped by delivery capacity. Pipeline 1 is Rs 800-900 crore and Pipeline 2 about Rs 3,500 crore, and the pipeline is growing.

qa_highlights.question: Will heavy structure be included in FY28 Rs 2,500 crore guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said HSS is assumed in that number, but it will update guidance after Q3 or Q4 of this year, once it has sales data.

qa_highlights.question: Why is OCF negative and when will it turn positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed larger milestone-based receivables and inventory build-up for the negative OCF, and expects it to turn positive quickly as it tightens payment terms.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin excluding one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said one-offs of Rs 5-6 crore would add about 0.25 percentage points, taking margin to about 9.7% from 9.3%.

risks_watch: Negative operating cash flow in FY26 and rising debtors; watch whether OCF turns positive in Q1 FY27.
Gujarat plant commercial production in July 2026 and Andhra heavy structure first sales (Rs 120-130 crore FY27 contribution) timing.
Steel price volatility: management said cyclical, with prices expected to soften from May-June; margin impact expected to be quarterly rather than annual.
Labour availability for construction sites flagged as the biggest challenge for FY27.
QIP fundraise (to be finalised within two to three months) and its size and use, mainly for heavy structures.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, capacity and order book, though cautious on near-term timelines (Gujarat delayed about a month) and explicit that guidance will be revised only after heavy structure sales begin. The tone was defensive on the Q4 sales shortfall and negative operating cash flow, which management attributed to seasonality, large-order milestones and inventory.
key_quotes: The capacities that we have are more or less fully utilized.
So, we are very happy with our results, as from a projected Rs. 1,720 crores, we have managed to do nearly Rs. 1,900 crores.
I think we are saying that Quarter 3 to Quarter 4, the growth has been 8.7%.
I think it is a very good margin if we can sustain it, because already we are spending money on building up the future business also.

adds.what: Gujarat PEB plant (fifth integrated plant, ~Rs 2,500 crore capacity) - trial production June, commercial production July 2026
Andhra Pradesh heavy structure plant - Phase 1 July-August 2026; full capacity 18,000-20,000 t/yr (Rs 200-210 crore)
Canadian JV 100% export unit (open web joist) under MoU signed 20 May 2026; plant ~Aug-Sep 2027

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided to Rs 2,150-2,200 crore (~13-16% growth, midpoint ~14.5%), backed by order book of over Rs 1,700 crore and Gujarat PEB plant (commercial production July 2026), with Andhra heavy structure plant from July-August, though the heavy structure revenue is not in the base figure and the plants are not yet running.
